chunk_findings.detail: The stub no longer emits `FAILED tests/test_x.py::…` lines after `=== short test summary info ===`, and the count line always prints `{n} failed`. Given `n=5` and argv `tests/test_x.py::test_a0`, the log is one `FAILED` line, then the summary header, then `5 failed in 0.1s`. A parser that reads node ids from the short summary (where the previous stub put them) records zero failures while the count says 5; a parser that counts `FAILED` lines records 1. The base-measurement path therefore cannot reproduce a baseline of the named failures, so this fixture does not exercise baseline-red auto-accept.

data.probe: Refuted on the same premise error as its rubber_duck counterpart: failed_tests() (ddflow/services/flakes.py:68-83) scans the WHOLE output text and matches _PYTEST_LINE (flakes.py:51-53) on ANY line, not only the short-summary section, so FAILED lines are harvested regardless of where they sit relative to the summary header. The n=5 one-id scenario in the finding is not what tests/test_gate_baseline_red.py::test_a_cut_full_suite_failure_is_still_measured_on_the_base runs: it uses n=55 with no argv (full run), so 55 distinct FAILED ids are harvested, kept aside (55 > MAX_FAILED_TESTS=50), re-run on the base, and the test asserts len(rec.evidence['baseline']['ids']) == 55 (the per-line list, not the summary count). python -m pytest -q tests/test_gate_baseline_red.py passes.
